scope: Structure only: concept titles, unit order and prerequisite intent. No third-party curriculum text is reproduced, and no restricted source is ingested.
description: An introductory chemistry course: atomic structure and periodicity, bonding and structure, quantitative chemistry, reactions and energetics, equilibrium, and organic and analytical chemistry.

concepts.title: States of matter and particle models
concepts.summary: The same particles arranged with different spacing and freedom of motion account for solids, liquids and gases.

concepts.title: Elements, compounds and mixtures
concepts.summary: The distinction is chemical: a compound's components are bonded, a mixture's are not.
prerequisites: States of matter and particle models

concepts.title: Physical and chemical changes
concepts.summary: A chemical change makes new substances while a physical change does not, even when appearance changes greatly.

concepts.title: Separation techniques
concepts.summary: Filtration, distillation and chromatography each exploit a different physical property difference.

concepts.title: Pure substances and purity testing
concepts.summary: A sharp melting point indicates purity while a range indicates contamination.

concepts.title: Atomic mass and relative masses
concepts.summary: Relative atomic mass is an average over natural isotopes weighted by abundance.

concepts.title: The mole and Avogadro's number
concepts.summary: A mole is a fixed count of particles, which lets chemists weigh out countable numbers of atoms.

concepts.title: Molar mass and mass-mole conversions
concepts.summary: Molar mass links the mass measured on a balance to the number of moles in the sample.

concepts.title: Concentration and molarity
concepts.summary: Concentration is amount of solute per volume of solution, and diluting changes volume not amount.

concepts.title: Empirical and molecular formulae
concepts.summary: Percentage composition gives the simplest ratio, and molar mass decides the multiple.

concepts.title: Percentage yield and atom economy
concepts.summary: Yield measures what you actually got; atom economy measures how much of the reactants ended up in the product.

concepts.title: Gas volumes and the ideal gas law
concepts.summary: At a given temperature and pressure equal volumes of gas contain equal numbers of particles.

concepts.title: Subatomic particles
concepts.summary: Protons, neutrons and electrons differ in charge and mass, and only protons define the element.

concepts.title: Atomic number, mass number and isotopes
concepts.summary: Atomic number counts protons and fixes identity; mass number counts protons plus neutrons.

concepts.title: Electron shells and energy levels
concepts.summary: Electrons occupy quantised shells, and chemical behaviour is governed by the outermost ones.

concepts.title: Electron configuration
concepts.summary: Filling order follows increasing energy, which is why the periodic table has the shape it does.

concepts.title: Emission spectra and evidence for levels
concepts.summary: Discrete spectral lines are direct evidence that electron energies are quantised.

concepts.title: Groups, periods and the table's structure
concepts.summary: Columns share outer-electron count and rows share shell count, which is why the table predicts behaviour.

concepts.title: Metals, non-metals and metalloids
concepts.summary: The dividing line between metals and non-metals explains the kinds of bonding each tends to form.
prerequisites: Groups, periods and the table's structure

concepts.title: Trends in atomic radius
concepts.summary: Radius falls across a period as nuclear charge grows and rises down a group as shells are added.
prerequisites: Groups, periods and the table's structure

concepts.title: Ionisation energy and electron affinity
concepts.summary: Ionisation energy measures how tightly an electron is held, so it rises across a period and falls down a group.

concepts.title: Group trends and reactivity
concepts.summary: Alkali metals become more reactive down the group while halogens become less, and both follow from outer-shell shielding.

concepts.title: Ionic bonding
concepts.summary: Electron transfer between a metal and a non-metal produces oppositely charged ions held in a lattice.

concepts.title: Covalent bonding
concepts.summary: Shared electron pairs hold non-metal atoms together, and the bond is directional.

concepts.title: Metallic bonding
concepts.summary: A sea of delocalised electrons explains why metals conduct and deform rather than shatter.

concepts.title: Dot-and-cross diagrams and Lewis structures
concepts.summary: Drawing outer electrons makes it visible whether an atom has achieved a stable count.

concepts.title: Bond polarity and electronegativity
concepts.summary: Unequal sharing creates a dipole, which is what makes many molecules reactive at specific sites.

concepts.title: Intermolecular forces
concepts.summary: London forces, dipole-dipole attractions and hydrogen bonding are much weaker than bonds but decide boiling points.

concepts.title: Giant covalent and simple molecular structures
concepts.summary: The same strong bonds give very different properties depending on whether they extend through the whole solid.

concepts.title: Shapes of molecules and VSEPR
concepts.summary: Electron pairs repel and arrange as far apart as possible, which predicts the shape and the bond angles.

concepts.title: Structure and physical properties
concepts.summary: Melting point, conductivity and solubility all follow from which particles are present and how they are held.
prerequisites: Giant covalent and simple molecular structures

concepts.title: Allotropes of carbon
concepts.summary: Diamond, graphite and graphene are all pure carbon yet differ completely because of how the atoms are arranged.

concepts.title: Nanoparticles and surface area
concepts.summary: Nanoparticles have a very large surface area to volume ratio, which changes their behaviour compared with bulk material.

concepts.title: Word and symbol equations
concepts.summary: A balanced symbol equation is a statement of conservation of atoms and charge.

concepts.title: Balancing chemical equations
concepts.summary: Coefficients must be adjusted so every element's count matches on both sides.

concepts.title: State symbols and reaction conditions
concepts.summary: State symbols and conditions carry real information that changes whether a reaction happens.

concepts.title: Ionic equations and spectator ions
concepts.summary: Removing ions that do not change reveals the actual reaction taking place.

concepts.title: Acids, bases and neutralisation
concepts.summary: An acid donates protons and a base accepts them, and neutralisation produces a salt and water.

concepts.title: pH and the hydrogen ion scale
concepts.summary: pH is a logarithmic measure of hydrogen ion concentration, so one unit is a tenfold change.

concepts.title: Strong and weak acids
concepts.summary: Strength refers to how completely an acid dissociates, which is different from concentration.
prerequisites: pH and the hydrogen ion scale

concepts.title: Titration and volumetric analysis
concepts.summary: A titration finds an unknown concentration by finding the exact volume that neutralises a known one.

concepts.title: Redox and oxidation states
concepts.summary: Redox reactions move electrons, and tracking oxidation states shows which species gained them.

concepts.title: Precipitation and solubility rules
concepts.summary: Mixing two solutions produces a solid when the ion combination is insoluble.

concepts.title: Reaction rates and collision theory
concepts.summary: Particles must collide with enough energy and the right orientation, which explains every rate factor.

concepts.title: Catalysts and activation energy
concepts.summary: A catalyst provides a lower-energy route without being consumed, so it does not change the equilibrium position.

concepts.title: Exothermic and endothermic reactions
concepts.summary: The sign of the enthalpy change says whether the system released or absorbed energy overall.

concepts.title: Bond energies and enthalpy change
concepts.summary: Breaking bonds costs energy and forming them releases it, and the net of the two sets the sign.

concepts.title: Energy level diagrams
concepts.summary: A reaction profile shows reactant and product energies and the activation hump between them.

concepts.title: Calorimetry and measuring enthalpy change
concepts.summary: A measured temperature rise plus a known heat capacity gives the energy released per mole.

concepts.title: Reversible reactions and dynamic equilibrium
concepts.summary: At equilibrium both directions continue at equal rates, so concentrations stop changing but nothing stops.

concepts.title: Le Chatelier's principle
concepts.summary: A system at equilibrium shifts to oppose the change imposed on it, which predicts the direction of shift.

concepts.title: The equilibrium constant
concepts.summary: The equilibrium constant summarises the position of equilibrium at a given temperature.

concepts.title: Factors affecting equilibrium position
concepts.summary: Concentration, pressure and temperature shift the position, while a catalyst only changes how fast it is reached.

concepts.title: Industrial equilibrium and yield optimisation
concepts.summary: The Haber process trades yield against rate, which is why real conditions are a compromise.

concepts.title: Carbon's bonding and catenation
concepts.summary: Carbon forms four strong bonds and bonds to itself, which is why there are millions of organic compounds.

concepts.title: Alkanes and saturated hydrocarbons
concepts.summary: Alkanes contain only single carbon-carbon bonds and are relatively unreactive.

concepts.title: Alkenes and unsaturation
concepts.summary: A carbon-carbon double bond makes alkenes reactive and lets them add atoms across the bond.

concepts.title: Homologous series and functional groups
concepts.summary: A functional group behaves consistently across a series, which is what makes organic chemistry predictable.

concepts.title: Naming organic compounds
concepts.summary: Systematic names encode chain length, functional group and position, so a name is a structure.

concepts.title: Isomerism
concepts.summary: The same molecular formula can give different structures, and different structures give different properties.

concepts.title: Alcohols and carboxylic acids
concepts.summary: The hydroxyl and carboxyl groups give these compounds their distinctive solubility, acidity and reactivity.

concepts.title: Polymers and polymerisation
concepts.summary: Addition and condensation routes build long chains from small monomers with different by-products.

concepts.title: Crude oil and fractional distillation
concepts.summary: Hydrocarbons separate by boiling point because chain length changes the strength of intermolecular forces.

concepts.title: Combustion of fuels
concepts.summary: Complete combustion gives carbon dioxide and water, while incomplete combustion gives carbon monoxide and soot.

concepts.title: Cracking and feedstock supply
concepts.summary: Cracking converts long, abundant chains into shorter, more useful ones including alkenes.

concepts.title: Greenhouse gases and climate effects
concepts.summary: Gases that absorb infrared radiation change the planet's energy balance, which changes climate.

concepts.title: Flame tests and cation identification
concepts.summary: Different metal ions emit characteristic colours, giving a quick identification test.

concepts.title: Testing for anions and gases
concepts.summary: Characteristic precipitates and gas reactions identify common anions and gases.

concepts.title: Paper and thin-layer chromatography
concepts.summary: Components travel at different rates according to how they partition, so they separate into spots.

concepts.title: Instrumental analysis
concepts.summary: Spectroscopy and spectrometry identify and quantify substances from how they interact with radiation.

concepts.title: Composition and evolution of the atmosphere
concepts.summary: The early atmosphere was largely carbon dioxide and water vapour, and photosynthesis changed that.

concepts.title: Air pollution and its chemistry
concepts.summary: Sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides form acid rain, and particulates affect health.
prerequisites: Composition and evolution of the atmosphere

concepts.title: Water treatment and purity
concepts.summary: Filtration, sedimentation and chlorination remove different classes of contaminant in sequence.
prerequisites: Composition and evolution of the atmosphere

concepts.title: Life cycle assessment and recycling
concepts.summary: Comparing products across their whole life cycle is more informative than comparing them at the point of use.
prerequisites: Composition and evolution of the atmosphere
